subject: Architecture
title: Cahokia: North America's Lost Metropolis
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cahokia: North America's Lost Metropolis.

hook.text: In 1100 AD, a city near modern St. Louis had more people than London at the same time.

buildup.text: Cahokia's Mississippian builders constructed 120 earthen mounds across six square miles.

discovery.text: Monks Mound is 100 feet tall and covers 14 acres — the largest earthwork in the Americas.

twist.text: The city had a wooden sun calendar — posts aligned to mark solstices and equinoxes with precision.

climax.text: Cahokia collapsed by 1400 AD. Deforestation, flooding, and political conflict likely contributed.

punchline.text: Medieval America's greatest city is now a state park most people drive past.

quiz.question: How does Monks Mound compare to other American earthworks?
options: It's the tallest but not the widest
It's the largest earthwork in the Americas
It's smaller than most Maya platforms

details.summary: Cahokia near present-day St. Louis was the largest pre-Columbian settlement north of Mexico, peaking at 10,000-20,000 residents around 1100 CE. Its centerpiece, Monks Mound, is the largest earthen structure in North America — taller than any building in the United States until 1867.
details.whyItMatters: Cahokia proves that complex urban civilization existed in North America centuries before European contact. Its scale challenges persistent myths that indigenous peoples lacked the capacity for monumental construction and city planning.
takeaways: Cahokia peaked at 10,000-20,000 people around 1100 CE
Monks Mound is North America's largest earthen structure
It was larger than contemporary London at its peak

faq.question: How big is Monks Mound?
faq.answer: The base covers 5.6 hectares — larger than the Great Pyramid at Giza. It rises 30 meters in four terraces, containing an estimated 622,000 cubic meters of earth moved entirely by hand in baskets. A massive wooden building once stood on top.

faq.question: Why did Cahokia decline?
faq.answer: Environmental degradation from deforestation, flooding from altered drainage, possible political instability, and climate shifts likely all contributed. The population dispersed gradually after 1200 CE. Little written history exists to explain the process in detail.
